# What Langfuse secret keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# A key is the prefix sk-lf- and a UUID, forty-two characters in all. The bodies
# here are the ordered run 0123456789abcdef written twice over with the
# separators a UUID puts through it, 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef, which
# no real credential is. It is spelled in lowercase where the case does not
# matter and in uppercase where the case is what a case is about: the
# hexadecimal is read in either.
#
# One case carries a body that is not that run, because what it turns on is a
# body the run cannot state: "a body of another version" writes the version and
# variant characters of the UUID it is about.
#
# What a key is written against, which characters a body may carry at which
# offset and where the scan settles are written out case by case in
# builtin_langfuse_secret_key_test.go. What is here is the pattern end to end
# through the public API, which is what this corpus is for.

patterns: langfuse-secret-key

# A key on its own, and the two places one is written. Langfuse issues a public
# key and a secret key together; only the secret key is redacted, the public key
# being the one Langfuse asks a caller to ship to every visitor.

case:     a key
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=«langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a key in json
in:       {"secretKey":"sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef"}
out:      {"secretKey":"«langfuse-secret-key»"}

# The hexadecimal is read in either case, and the version of the UUID is not
# read at all: Langfuse mints a key from a version 4 UUID, and a scan reading
# that would locate nothing were Langfuse to change generators.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89AB-CDEF-0123-456789ABCDEF
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

case:     a body of another version
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-7def-9123-456789abcdef
out:      «langfuse-secret-key»

# What is left alone. A body one character short of the count is the shape a
# line cut to a column limit leaves; the four separators standing where a UUID
# puts them are the whole of what tells a body from thirty-six other characters
# behind the prefix; and the prefix is read as Langfuse writes it.

case:     a body one character short of the count
in:       sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcde
out:      sk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcde

case:     a separator one character in front of where a uuid puts it
in:       sk-lf-0123456-789ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      sk-lf-0123456-789ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       SK-LF-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      SK-LF-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

# The public key, which Langfuse publishes by design: its browser SDK takes that
# key and nothing else, and its docs write it into a name Next.js compiles into
# what the browser downloads.

case:     the public key on its own
in:       LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
